facts.statement: The genus Utahceratops was first named by Scott D. Sampson and six other researchers in 2010.
facts.quote: It was first named by Scott D. Sampson, Mark A. Loewen, Andrew A. Farke, Eric M. Roberts, Catherine A. Forster, Joshua A. Smith and Alan L. Titus in 2010

facts.statement: Utahceratops was a large, robust quadrupedal herbivore that could grow to an estimated length of 4.5 to 5 meters.
facts.quote: Utahceratops was a large-sized, robustly-built, ground-dwelling, quadrupedal herbivore, that could grow up to an estimated 4.5 - 5 m long.

facts.statement: Utahceratops is estimated to have weighed approximately 2 tonnes.
facts.quote: Utahceratops are estimated to have measured 4.5 - 5 m in length and 2 tonne in weight.

facts.statement: Utahceratops possessed short, robust supraorbital horncores that were blunt-tipped and directed dorsolaterally.
facts.quote: the supraorbital horncores are short, robust, dorsolaterally directed, and oblate in shape with a blunt tip

facts.statement: The lateral frill of Utahceratops featured extremely elongate episquamosals, some measuring over 10 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: the episquamosals on the mid-portion of the lateral frill margin are low and extremely elongate (some >10 cm long)

facts.statement: Six specimens of Utahceratops are known, preserving about 96% of the skull and 70% of the postcranial skeleton.
facts.quote: This genus is known from six specimens, including two partial skulls, which when taken together preserve about 96% of the skull and 70% of the postcranial skeleton.

facts.statement: Utahceratops lived approximately 76.4 to 75.5 million years ago in what is now Utah.
facts.quote: Utahceratops is an extinct genus of ceratopsian dinosaur that lived approximately 76.4~75.5 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Utah.

facts.statement: The habitat of Utahceratops was an ancient floodplain dominated by channels, wetland peat swamps, ponds, and lakes, bordered by highlands.
facts.quote: The plateau where dinosaurs lived was an ancient floodplain dominated by large channels and abundant wetland peat swamps, ponds and lakes, and was bordered by highlands.

facts.statement: Utahceratops is classified as a basal chasmosaurine ceratopsian.
facts.quote: Utahceratops has been classified as a basal chasmosaurine ceratopsian.

facts.statement: Utahceratops is found in a clade of basal chasmosaurines that includes Pentaceratops.
facts.quote: It has been found to be in a clade of basal chasmosaurines with Pentaceratops.

facts.statement: The name Utahceratops means "horned face from Utah", derived from the state name and Greek words for horn and face.
facts.quote: The genus name Utahceratops, means "horned face from Utah", and is derived from the state of Utah and Greek words "keras" (κέρας) meaning "horn" and "ops" (ὤψ) referring to the "face".

facts.statement: The specific name gettyi honors Mike Getty, who discovered the holotype and aided in fossil recovery from the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument.
facts.quote: The specific name gettyi, is derived from the name of Mike Getty, who discovered the holotype and has played a pivotal role in the recovery of fossils from the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument (GSENM).

facts.statement: Utahceratops shared its environment with diverse dinosaurs including dromaeosaurids, tyrannosaurids like Teratophoneus, ankylosaurids, hadrosaurs like Parasaurolophus and Gryposaurus, and other ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Utahceratops shared its paleoenvironment with other dinosaurs, such as dromaeosaurid theropods, the troodontid Talos sampsoni, tyrannosaurids like Teratophoneus, armored ankylosaurids, the duckbilled hadrosaurs Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus and Gryposaurus monumentensis, the ceratopsians Nasutoceratops titusi and Kosmoceratops richardsoni and the oviraptorosaurian Hagryphus giganteus.

facts.statement: The paleofauna of the Kaiparowits Formation included chondrichthyans (sharks and rays), amphibians, turtles, lizards, and crocodilians.
facts.quote: La paleofauna presente en la Formación Kaiparowits incluía condrictios, tiburones y rayas, ranas, salamandras , tortugas , lagartos y cocodrilos.

facts.statement: Primitive mammals, including multituberculates, marsupials, and insectivorans, were present in the Kaiparowits Formation.
facts.quote: Una variedad de mamíferos primitivos estuvo presente incluyendo multituberculados, marsupiales e insectívoros.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Albertosaurus and Ornithomimus velox were present in the Kaiparowits Formation, as existing fossil evidence is not conclusive.
facts.quote: Some fossil evidence suggests the presence of the tyrannosaurid Albertosaurus and the ornithomimid Ornithomimus velox, but the existing assessment of the material is not conclusive.

rejected.statement: The only known specimen of Utahceratops was recovered from the Kaiparowits Formation in Utah.
rejected.quote: The only known specimen of Utahceratops was recovered at the Kaiparowits Formation, in Utah.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'The only known specimen of Utahceratops was recovered'

rejected.statement: The Kaiparowits Formation, where Utahceratops fossils were found, was deposited between 76.6 and 74.5 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
rejected.quote: Argon-argon radiometric dating indicates that the Kaiparowits Formation was deposited between 76.6 and 74.5 million years ago, during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'was deposited between 76.6 and 74.5 million years'

rejected.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, the Kaiparowits Formation was located near the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway, which separated North America into Laramidia and Appalachia.
rejected.quote: During the Late Cretaceous period, the site of the Kaiparowits Formation was located near the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway, a large inland sea that split North America into two landmasses, Laramidia to the west and Appalachia to the east.
